text:
sam-cs: Customer report: EU enterprise tenant seeing 4xx/5xx spikes and 200-400ms extra latency since ~09:10 UTC. They say requests are being billed from us-west-2. Can ops confirm routing?
support-sally: Copy. Their org id is org_8675309, sample req ids in ticket. They get occasional 401 then long tails.
maria-infra: Looking at routing logs for org_8675309... initial hits go to eu-west-1 but when capacity drops we see a fallback to us-west-2 LB for some tokens. :thinking:
kevin-oncall: Paging @maria-infra and @ops-bot — is there an active rollout of cross-region fallback policy?
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4583 assigned to kevin-oncall. PagerDuty alert linked.
maria-infra: We rolled a change to routing-policy v3.2 at 09:05 UTC to enable region-fallback for latency smoothing. The rollout used dynamic rules that match tenant workload patterns. I see a condition that incorrectly treats short-lived auth failures as capacity signals.
sam-cs: Customer says they never opted into cross-region routing (data residency concern). They were promised EU-only for this contract.
kevin-oncall: Can we reproduce? curl example from customer: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n  -H "X-Target-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -d '{"model":"gptx-8k","prompt":"hi"}'
```
They still observe backend showing us-west-2 in the request log.
maria-infra: Querying router logs: 
```
2026-03-15T09:11:02Z req=abc123 org=org_8675309 routed_to=us-west-2 reason=fallback_policy(health_signal)
2026-03-15T09:11:05Z req=abc124 org=org_8675309 auth_status=200 token=valid
```
The fallback decision fired even though token checks passed. Bug in evaluation order.
product-amy: This is important for EU compliance customers. We need to revert routing-policy ASAP and notify affected customers.
kevin-oncall: Rolling back v3.2 now. Triggering canary abort and full rollback.
deploy-bot: Rollback started for routing-policy v3.2 by kevin-oncall at 09:18 UTC.
maria-infra: Rollback complete on control plane at 09:21 UTC. Confirming region pinning is back for org_8675309.
support-sally: I'm telling the customer it's been reverted and asking for validation.
sam-cs: Customer confirms: subsequent requests show eu-west-1 and latency normalized. They still want an explanation and postmortem.
kevin-oncall: Short post-incident notes: impact window ~09:05-09:21 UTC. Affected: 1 enterprise tenant, increased latency and occasional 401-like failures due to mismatched routing path. Root cause: rollback-safe check in routing policy evaluated auth signal after fallback conditions; a timing race caused fallback to trigger on transient probe failures.
product-amy: Action items: (1) Add unit + integration test to ensure auth status is consulted before fallback (owner: maria-infra), (2) Add tenant region residency flag that is enforced at control-plane (owner: product-amy), (3) Alerting: create a metric for cross-region fallback rate per-tenant and alert threshold (owner: kevin-oncall).
maria-infra: I'll open PR for reorder of checks and add test coverage. Also proposing a safety gate for rollouts that verifies residency constraints for contracts marked EU-only.
kevin-oncall: Filing formal postmortem doc and customer-facing summary. Draft will land in #incidents-docs.
support-sally: Customer-facing note ready; will send after PM review.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-4583 resolved at 09:21 UTC. Follow-ups tracked in tasks: RACK-1345, RACK-1346, RACK-1347.
product-amy: Thanks team. For transparency, let's run a sweep of other tenants with region pinning to ensure no similar rollouts slipped through. :eyes: 
kevin-oncall: Agreed. I'll run a query to list tenants with pinning and confirm no other hits in logs during rollout window.
sam-cs: Marking this thread for postmortem inclusion.
